Message Pattern Specifications provide a succinct and disciplined mechanism to specify and enforce run-time object behaviour, and to handle errors that occur during execution.

(1) the specification of the run-time behaviour of a system of objects is an orthogonal and disciplined approach to error handling in object oriented systems; and (2) this approach is particularly useful in parallel object oriented programming, since it allows for the specification of the 'legal' run-time behaviours of the objects in the system, and the methods that the system should invoke to recover from errors.

Message Pattern Specifications (or MPS) are a new technique for specifying the legal run-time patterns of interaction between objects, and for defining recovery or graceful failure methods in the event that these patterns are violated.
